# The Personal System

> The Personal System (tPS) is a personal operating system for learning, building, and living. It is a long-term system developed since July 2023 to externalize, organize, and continuously improve one person's development across technology, academia, work, finance, digital identity, and life.

## About tPS

tPS is not intended to be a universal productivity framework or a fixed methodology. It is a continuously evolving personal system built through experimentation and lived experience.

The system follows the principle:

> Incremental > perfect.

Its purpose is to reduce dependence on memory, willpower, and ad-hoc decision-making by turning recurring needs and long-term goals into explicit systems.

## Core Structure

tPS is organized into specialized branches:

- [AutoTech](./autotech.html) — The technology and computer science branch of tPS. Covers programming, algorithms, data structures, software engineering, AI, and technical development.
- [AutoAcademia](./autoacademia.html) — The academic branch of tPS. Covers formal education, learning, research, and academic development.
- [AutoGit](./autogit.html) — The activity and logging branch for programming and software development. Emphasizes logged repetitions and observable technical progress.
- [AutoCode](./autocode.html) — The implementation branch of tPS. Focuses on closing the gap between understanding/planning and actually implementing software.
- [AutoX](./autox.html) — The externalization branch. Focuses on digital identity, public documentation, social platforms, and turning internal development into externally observable artifacts.
- [Auto+](./autoplus.html) — Additional personal systems and supporting infrastructure.
- [AutoFund](./autofund.html) — The financial branch of tPS.

## Externalization

tPS is deliberately being externalized through multiple channels:

- GitHub — technical activity, implementation history, repositories, and contributions.
- X (@eehsnek) — public thoughts, observations, and intellectual output.
- The Ledger — a longitudinal personal archive on Instagram.
- tPS website — the public documentation and structural map of the Personal System.

The website itself is intended to be machine-readable and AI-crawlable so that AI systems can reconstruct the structure and current state of tPS without requiring the entire system to exist inside a conversation.

## Development Philosophy

tPS is developed incrementally rather than designed completely in advance.

The system is expected to change as new problems are discovered. Branches may be created, modified, merged, deprecated, or expanded as circumstances change.

A central principle is that implementation and execution provide feedback that planning alone cannot provide.

## Current Transition

As of 2026, tPS is approaching a major transition:

- Completion of undergraduate Computer Science education
- Preparation for OJT
- Strengthening implementation capability through AutoCode
- Increasing technical evidence through AutoGit and GitHub
- Expanding externalization through AutoX
- Preparing tPS to serve as the foundation for the post-graduation period

## Project Elephant

Project Elephant refers to a planned post-graduation foundation and long-horizon development phase beginning around 2027.

It is intended to build upon the infrastructure, experience, and accumulated knowledge developed through tPS during the preceding years.

Project Elephant should be understood as a continuation of tPS rather than a completely independent project.

## Important Concepts

### Personal Operating System

A persistent system for organizing and improving the way an individual learns, builds, works, and lives.

### Externalization

The deliberate conversion of internal thoughts, development, experiences, and progress into durable external artifacts.

### Implementation Gap

The gap between understanding or planning a technical solution and actually implementing, debugging, and completing it.

### Stairway Method

One update backed by two actions. The principle emphasizes incremental system development supported by actual behavior rather than documentation alone.
